name: Non-syndromic Multisutural Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Multisutural Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal skull shape due to premature fusion of two or more cranial sutures without associated syndromic features
CT scan or 3D imaging demonstrating premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic craniosynostosis (e.g., no limb anomalies, normal genetic testing for syndromic mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal skull shape with radiological confirmation of multiple suture fusion and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic forms; diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures
searchTerms: early fusion of multiple skull bones

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal cranial vault shape with brachycephaly or scaphocephaly
searchTerms: abnormal skull shape with short or long head
raised lines on skull where bones joined

common.symptomName: Increased intracranial pressure signs (e.g., irritability, vomiting)

searchTerms: delayed closing of soft spot on head

rare.symptomName: Visual impairment due to optic nerve compression
searchTerms: vision loss from optic nerve pressure
blurred vision due to nerve compression

imaging: CT scan with 3D reconstruction showing premature fusion of multiple cranial sutures
MRI to assess intracranial pressure and brain development
genetic: Negative for mutations in FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, TWIST1 genes associated with syndromic craniosynostosis
other: Physical examination revealing palpable suture ridging and abnormal skull shape

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of limb anomalies or other systemic features
Positive genetic testing for syndromic mutations

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., vomiting, irritability)
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: diagnosis, evaluation, and management. 3rd edition. Oxford University Press; 2000.
Wilkie AO, Morriss-Kay GM. Genetics of craniofacial development and malformation. Nat Rev Genet. 2001;2(6):458-68.
